subject: Shelf credit acceleration & dynamic reallocation proposal
messages:
From: Sarah Bennett <sarah.bennett@voltedge.com>
To: aisha_rahman@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Tom O'Neill <tom.oneill@voltedge.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Shelf credit acceleration request + drawdown model

Hi Aisha,

Thanks again for the call earlier — VoltEdge is interested in a multi-year committed spend with a prepay wallet structure, but we need clarity on two operational pieces before we can move to procurement:

1) Acceleration triggers: we expect occasional spikes. Can Redwood define a clear mechanism where credits can be accelerated from the shelf to cover spikes without resetting our committed term? Specifically: what triggers, how quickly credits are made available, and how those accelerated draws affect remaining committed buckets.

2) Dynamic reallocation / underutilization: if we underutilize an early tranche in year 1, what's the process and timing to reallocate that capacity into later tranches (instead of forfeiture)? We need a reconciliation cadence and a lookback window.

From our side we are leaning toward a 24-month ARR-style commit with front-loaded prepay for the first 3 months (accelerated ramp), then monthly drawdowns. We have attached our RFQ and an example usage profile.

Please attach a short example drawdown table and a concise description of any pricing impact for an acceleration event. Procurement will need a one-page term summary for legal.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call if helpful.

—Sarah
Sarah Bennett
Head of Cloud Ops, VoltEdge
[sent with attachment: Voltedge_RFQ_0826.pdf]

From: aisha_rahman@redwoodinference.com
To: Sarah Bennett <sarah.bennett@voltedge.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com, marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-08-31T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Shelf credit acceleration request + drawdown model

Sarah — thanks for the clear ask and the RFQ. Attached is a short draft (redwood_proposal_draft_0828.pdf) and an example drawdown table. High-level summary below, and I’ve looped Lauren (finance) and Marcus (sales ops) for the operational and accounting details.

Summary proposal (high-level)
- Structure: 24-month committed wallet with monthly drawdown windows; initial 3-month accelerated ramp funded up-front as a prepay tranche.
- Acceleration trigger: automatic temporary acceleration allowance up to 50% of the next tranche if observed monthly usage > 2.5x forecast for two consecutive days. Acceleration is billed against the prepay wallet immediately; any over-usage beyond wallet drains will move to standard overage rates.
- Reallocation / underutilization: 90-day lookback reconciliation window each quarter. Underutilized credits from a prior tranche may be moved into a subsequent tranche once per quarter subject to a 10% administrative reallocation fee (waivable at higher commit tiers).
- Pricing impact: tiered term discount on committed units — 12% for 12 months, 18% for 24 months (applied to committed wallet when funded). Acceleration does not change discount level; overages billed at pay-as-you-go rate.

Open items for procurement/legal
- Exact wording for acceleration clause and definition of a usage "spike" (we can provide precise metric language).
- Reallocation fee waiver conditions.
- Early termination / credit refunds (prorated with a 60-day notice and a recapture schedule).

Can you confirm: 1) VoltEdge is targeting a 24-month legal term? 2) Are you OK with the 90-day quarterly reconciliation cadence? If yes, we’ll produce a one-page term summary for procurement and a redline-ready term sheet for legal.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 20-min call tomorrow to align.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
[attached: redwood_proposal_draft_0828.pdf]

From: lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com
To: aisha_rahman@redwoodinference.com, marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-09-01T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Shelf credit acceleration request + drawdown model

Looping in finance notes and proposed redlines so Aisha can share a clean term summary with VoltEdge. See comments inline below and quick bullets: 

—Lauren (Finance) bullets—
- Exposure cap: propose a maximum unlocked-acceleration exposure equal to 150% of the funded wallet for the first 6 months; after month 6 we reduce to 100% to limit credit risk.
- Accounting / amortization: prepay wallet will be amortized monthly over the committed term for revenue recognition; we need the funded dates clearly on the term summary to align with your accounting team.
- Reallocation admin fee: suggest 5% instead of 10% for enterprise customers, and an auto-waive if usage growth > 20% quarter-over-quarter (helps keep the deal moving).
- Early termination: carveout for acquisition / force majeure with a negotiated recapture schedule (we should keep language standard; legal to confirm).

—Marcus (Sales Ops) quick ops note—
- Add a 14-day notification window for planned large bursts that would request manual temporary top-ups from the dedicated pool. This prevents surprise auto-acceleration events.
- Recommend we offer an optional "buffer reserve" add-on (10% of monthly committed volume) for a small premium; VoltEdge can opt in on month 1.

I added karty (Karthik) for model impact on routing/capacity planning — Karthik, please confirm whether buffer reserve requires a different placement rule in our Dedicated pools.

—Quoted from Aisha's email for context—
> Acceleration trigger: automatic temporary acceleration allowance up to 50% of the next tranche if observed monthly usage > 2.5x forecast for two consecutive days.

I'll prepare a 1-pager with the financial bullets and suggested legal language; Aisha, once you get Sarah's confirmation we'll finalize.

Thanks,
Lauren
VP, Revenue Finance
Redwood Inference

From: Sarah Bennett <sarah.bennett@voltedge.com>
To: aisha_rahman@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Tom O'Neill <tom.oneill@voltedge.com>
Date: 2026-09-02T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Shelf credit acceleration request + drawdown model

Aisha — thanks for the quick turnaround and for looping in finance. VoltEdge is prepared to move forward on a conditional basis. Our procurement checklist requires two items before legal: 1) a one-page term summary and 2) a sample drawdown table that shows month-by-month balances with the acceleration event applied. Both look fine in your draft, but we need the following clarifications to finalize commercially:

- Term & discount: we will accept a 24-month term at the 18% term discount, provided there is a 90-day reallocation window and the 5% reallocation admin fee (per Lauren) is applied.
- Acceleration exposure cap: agree to the staged exposure cap (150% first 6 months, 100% thereafter) but would like the 14-day planned-burst notification to be included as an operational exception.
- Buffer reserve: VoltEdge would like the optional 10% buffer reserve, but please include pricing as a per-month line item so we can present to finance as an optional add-on.

If Redwood can produce the one-page summary and the sample drawdown table with those exact bullets called out, VoltEdge procurement will circulate the term summary and move to DocuSign. Benign legal redlines expected. Please send the one-pager and sample table and we’ll route immediately.

We’ll plan to sign contingent on that one-page summary.

—Sarah
Head of Cloud Ops, VoltEdge
[sent with attachment: redwood_term_summary_0829.pdf]
